# Frozen whitepapers

**Do not edit anything in this directory, and do not point a generator at it.**

Each file is `docs/compost.md` exactly as it stood at the tag in its name. They
are historical documents: every one contains statements that were true when
written and are false now — `compost-v0.2.12.md` says there are ten invariants
and describes a conditional per-node `content_hash`, both of which v0.2.13
replaced.

**Why copies exist when git already has them.** `git show v0.2.11:docs/compost.md`
reconstructs any of these exactly, so this directory is not the history — it is
the history made *ingestible*. The point is to digest every version into a base
once v0.2.17 lands `revision_of`, and get a real revision chain over the
document this project uses to explain itself. A tool that had to shell out to
git to find its own inputs would be a worse tool.

**The current whitepaper is `docs/compost.md`, and its path never moves.**
`tools/build_whitepaper.py`, `tests/test_grammar.py` and `tests/test_manpage.py`
all hardcode it. Versioning the *live* file's name would move three call sites
every release, and — worse — whatever was left at `docs/compost.md` would have
its appendix regenerated by the build, silently rewriting a frozen snapshot. So
the version lives in the document's title, not in its filename, and only the
frozen copies here carry a version in their names.

**Adding one**, when a release ships:

    git show vX.Y.Z:docs/compost.md > docs/whitepaper/compost-vX.Y.Z.md

Do it *after* the tag exists, and never from the working tree — by then the
working copy has already moved on. `docs/compost.md` at the time of writing was
no longer a clean v0.2.12 snapshot for exactly that reason.
